title: Nuclear severe-accident correction requires design-basis humility, operating-experience memory, and emergency information rails
summary: A candidate pattern for severe nuclear-accident correction. Supporting records are TMI, Chornobyl/Chernobyl, Fukushima Daiichi, and nuclear operating-experience/notification rails. The pattern is about how design-basis assumptions, instrumentation, safety culture/regulation, emergency preparation, and lesson-infusion surfaces are stress-tested—not a verdict on nuclear power as a whole.

status_history.note: Created after promoting TMI, Chornobyl/Chernobyl, Fukushima Daiichi, IRSNI, and IAEA emergency notification records.

subjects.name: nuclear severe-accident correction and design-basis humility

claims.claim: Three Mile Island, Chornobyl/Chernobyl, and Fukushima Daiichi support a candidate pattern in which severe nuclear accidents expose the limits of design-basis assumptions, instrumentation legibility, emergency procedures, safety culture/regulatory structure, and operating-experience loops.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: Nuclear operating-experience and emergency-notification rails—IRSNI, USIE/NEWS, and the Early Notification Convention—make parts of correction memory and public significance more legible, but their existence does not prove that lessons are infused into plant design, operations, regulation, or emergency practice.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

evidence_refs.support_type: emergency notification and public information rail

claims.claim: This pattern remains candidate-only and rejects two crude inferences: that nuclear accidents are explained by operators alone, and that the lane proves a general pro- or anti-nuclear verdict. The record grain is sociotechnical correction history, not ideology.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: MKH-PAT-0018 is adjacent to existing proof-burden/warning-governance and correction-memory-versus-infusion patterns, but it should not be merged until controls show whether nuclear severe accidents require a domain-specific pattern or are instances of a more general sociotechnical failure family.

evidence_refs.support_type: correction memory versus correction infusion family

evidence_profile.source_depth: derived from three promoted engineering records, two infrastructure records, and one-pass official sources; no controls promoted
limitations: No comparative denominator for nuclear energy risk, non-nuclear energy risk, or regulator-by-regulator practice.

positive_controls_needed: A nuclear near-miss or event where operating-experience memory demonstrably prevented recurrence.
A plant/regulator change record showing a design-basis or severe-accident-management lesson infused into equipment, procedures, exercises, and inspection before a stressor occurred.
negative_controls_needed: A severe nuclear event where design-basis or OPEX rails were present but not explanatory.
A high-risk non-nuclear system with similar external-hazard design-basis challenge to test whether this is nuclear-specific or a general engineered-system pattern.
counterexamples_to_seek: Cases where strong safety culture and conservative design-basis assumptions prevented event escalation.
Evidence that the three cases should be split into separate patterns: instrumentation/human factors, reactor-design/regulatory framework, and external-hazard/multi-unit stress.
rollback_triggers: If future source review shows these cases are too heterogeneous for one pattern.
If the pattern is used as a simplistic pro-/anti-nuclear claim rather than a correction-history scaffold.
If controls show correction rails, not design-basis humility, are the real common axis.

maturity_gate.minimum_cases: 3 supporting records plus 2 positive controls plus 2 negative controls
maturity_gate.required_evidence: official investigation/report sources, regulator follow-through, operating-experience evidence, emergency-communication evidence, and explicit non-ideological scope limits

handling_notes: Do not use the pattern as a pro-/anti-nuclear ideology token.
Avoid casualty spectacle and community-trauma flattening.
Keep operator/design/regulator/organizational causation separate and source-bounded.

unknowns: No positive or negative controls have been promoted.
No recommendation-closure or practice-infusion child records are attached.
No comparative energy-risk denominator or regulator-by-regulator audit is attached.
next_actions: Add a nuclear near-miss or intercepted-event positive control.
Add recommendation-closure child records for TMI, Chornobyl/Chernobyl, and Fukushima Daiichi.
Compare with non-nuclear external-hazard/design-basis failures such as chemical plants, dams, offshore drilling, and electrical grids.
